targets.review_note: For every horizontal scanline inside the vertical span of a connected simple orthogonal polygon, exactly its leftmost and rightmost boundary intersections are visible from the two horizontal directions. Integrating gives visible vertical-wall length twice the height span, regardless of concavities. The vertical-scanline analogue gives twice the width span. Subtract these exposed lengths from the Manhattan perimeter; vertex-level ties have zero length and do not affect the measure.

targets.review_note: Expand the final product by assigning each selected increment factor to the operation that produced it. Partition selected positions into r nonempty blocks sharing an operation; a block contributes its smallest position divided by n. Scan positions increasingly: taking a constant contributes a_j; joining one of r existing blocks contributes r*v without changing its minimum; opening a block contributes j*v. Thus dp_j[r]=(a_j+r*v)*dp_previous[r]+j*v*dp_previous[r-1]. Finally assign distinct operation labels via the falling factorial(m)_r and divide by n^r. Truncate only mathematically impossible r>m, not model input or answers.
